claims.text: A deep-learning potential trained on targeted high-temperature ab initio data can substantially reduce the cost of predicting fusion and high-temperature thermodynamic properties.
The proposed deep-learning potential can maintain accuracy while reducing computational cost.
The deep-learning potential can implicitly capture vibrational entropy, anharmonicity, and electron–vibration coupling effects.
Full explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics free-energy evaluations would be replaced by a surrogate deep-learning potential trained on representative ab initio data.
Learning from ab initio free energies allows the potential to encode the relevant high-temperature energy landscape.
Encoding the energy landscape enables implicit representation of vibrational, anharmonic, and electron–vibration coupling effects.
Mapping the complex free-energy surface with a carefully chosen training set allows the model to reproduce essential thermodynamic observables.
Surrogate-model evaluation accelerates simulations relative to explicit ab initio molecular dynamics.
The method will predict phase free energies with fidelity comparable to explicit ab initio molecular dynamics.
The method will predict phase free energies with fidelity comparable to TOR-TILD.
For elemental and binary systems, the method will reduce simulation time by approximately one order of magnitude.
The method will scale better than the baseline workflows for complex multicomponent systems.
Explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics free-energy calculations and TOR-TILD are computationally demanding, particularly for high-entropy multicomponent systems.
Initial validation is restricted to elemental and binary systems near their melting points.
Extension to high-entropy or other compositionally complex alloys requires caution and additional validation.
Reliable treatment of electron–vibration coupling in multicomponent systems depends on training data covering the broader composition and temperature range.

The model is to be benchmarked against explicit ab initio molecular dynamics and TOR-TILD using solid–fluid phase free-energy differences, melting temperatures, vibrational entropy, and anharmonicity markers.
A discrepancy greater than 5% from explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics or TOR-TILD values across the evaluated conditions would falsify the hypothesis.
